reattach.source: not implemented; provider reattach surface verified present
reattach.reason: Corrected 2026-08-20. This cell previously read upstream_absent on the grounds that Antigravity exposed no stable reattach surface. That was true of the 1.1.5 observation it was written against and is false now: `agy --conversation <id>` resumes an existing conversation with intact history, including after the previous process was killed with SIGINT. Verified against 1.1.16. Longhouse has not built the reattach path.

send_input.source: real agy --print PreInvocation hook-inbox injection changed the model-visible turn
send_input.reason: Proven live by scripts/qa/provider-control-e2e-canary.py --antigravity-real-agy-send: a queued message is claimed at PreInvocation, the inbox drains, and the injected text replaces the model-visible turn. Availability follows the hook rather than the release, because hooks do not fire under GEMINI_API_KEY auth -- the control fact's granted_operations is empty whenever the hook has not been seen recently, so a healthy but uncontrollable session offers nothing.

interrupt.source: no native cancel; reconstructable as kill plus resume
interrupt.reason: Antigravity exposes no native turn cancel. `user` is the only accepted stream-json input event -- interrupt, cancel, stop and abort are all rejected as unsupported -- and SIGINT ends the process rather than the turn. The conversation survives and resumes intact by id, so interrupt is reconstructable as kill-then-resume rather than natively supported. Typing it as a native interrupt would be a lie to the caller.
interrupt.owner_action: antigravity kill-and-resume interrupt path with process-group reap

steer_active_turn.source: not implemented; bounded injection verified against 1.1.16
steer_active_turn.reason: Corrected 2026-08-20. Bounded active-turn injection is proven, not unproven: a message queued in the hook inbox is claimed at the next PreInvocation inside the running turn and changes the model's course before that turn ends. Steering lands at an invocation boundary, so a single long tool call delays it -- it is bounded, not immediate, and product copy must say so. Longhouse does not route to it.

answer_pause.reason: Headless Antigravity never pauses for a permission or a question. It reports permission_mode always-proceed and settles the choice itself, which upstream made deliberate in 1.1.12. There is no pause to answer. The Helm TUI does prompt but exposes no structured surface for it, so answering would mean scraping and driving a PTY.

terminate.source: unsupported until process termination policy is designed
terminate.reason: SIGINT ends the process cleanly and emits a typed error result, but leaves run_command children orphaned. Longhouse has not designed the process-group termination policy that requires, and shipping terminate without it would strand child processes on every kill.
terminate.owner_action: antigravity process termination policy and canary

turn_start.source: real agy executed with the Console adapter's own argv, read from the engine, returning a structured result at the transcript path the adapter binds
turn_start.reason: One bounded `agy --print` invocation per Console turn. This path does not use hooks, which is why it matters: hook delivery is unavailable under GEMINI_API_KEY auth, so the Console turn is the control surface that works under either credential authority. The canary now reads the argv from `longhouse-engine antigravity-console-argv` instead of rebuilding it, so the adapter's command line, the result shape it parses, and the transcript path it binds are all proven against the installed release. It refuses to run rather than falling back to a copy when the engine is unavailable.
